Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the RAG evaluation scope: 

Summary of needs
- Support for product docs + user-generated content as knowledge sources (mix of PDFs + SQL-exported text)
- High emphasis on grounding (false-positive hallucinations are a showstopper)
- Latency target: 200-300ms P95 for single-threaded web requests; throughput expected ~50 qps initially
- Quality: prefer slightly higher precision in top-3 results vs pure recall

Redwood recommendations (initial)
1) Retriever: dense dual-encoder (FAISS HNSW) over sparse/BM25 for mixed-format content; run a small BM25 baseline to surface token-match issues.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder (distil-cross-encoder) for top-50 -> re-rank to top-5; this keeps grounding precision high.
3) Model choices: provide two serving profiles —
   - High-quality: redwood/gpt-neoxt-20b (quant8, cross-attn optimizations) + cross-encoder reranker
   - Cost-optimized: redwood/llama-2-70b-quant (4-bit) + stronger reranker thresholding
4) Evaluation set: use ACME prompt set v2 (attached), add 120 business-critical queries from your support logs for regression monitoring.
5) Grounding metrics: grounding rate (percentage of answers with at least one exact source link), top-1 factual precision, and hallucination rate via spot-checking.

Attachments: I attached a starter benchmark workbook (acme-benchmarks-202705.xlsx) and the prompt sets (acme-prompt-sets-v2.jsonl). Also linking our eval template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqAcme-RAG-eval

Asks / next steps
- Jordan: can you confirm the 120 query list and share a representative set of documents (PDFs or S3 URIs)?
- Priya: are there any compliance constraints around storing embeddings in a managed index? If so we can propose a private index pattern.
- We'll kick off a small benchmark job once we have data (timeline ~3 business days to get initial numbers).

I'll loop Aditya on the technical plan and Marcus on post-deployment monitoring. Happy to run a 30-minute deep-dive next week if useful.

Best,

Thanks for the context — some quick technical notes based on the sample and constraints: 

- Elastic vs FAISS: Elastic/BM25 is fast and cheap, and worth keeping as a fallback. For mixed PDFs and paraphrased queries, dense retrieval (bi-encoder with FAISS HNSW) usually raises recall enough that downstream reranker has better candidates. We can run both in parallel for the baseline and do ablation.

- Two-stage rerank strategy (recommended):
  1) Bi-encoder embed candidate set (top-200) — extremely cheap using a distilled bi-encoder.
  2) Apply a cross-encoder only to top-50 from step 1 for final ranking. This gets most of the cross-encoder gains at a fraction of cost.

- Reranker models: start with distil-cross-encoder (good latency/cost tradeoff) and have a fall-back heavier cross-encoder for high-risk queries (legal/financial).

- Grounding metrics definition: 
  * Grounding Rate: percent of answers with at least one matched doc id + exact sentence source link.
  * Top-1 Factual Precision: of answers labeled correct by SMEs, percent where factual claims are traceable to source text.
  * Hallucination Rate: percent of answers with claims contradicted by any source in top-5.

- Retrieval settings to try in initial benchmark: HNSW ef_search=128, ef_construction=200, index dim=768 (distil-bi-encoder) and an Elastic BM25 run with default analyzer for baseline. Reranker threshold: only promote cross-encoder results when bi-encoder score margin < 0.08.

Operational notes: we can deliver a small benchmark run (both retriever flavors + two reranker configs + two model profiles) within ~4 business days once you share the 120 queries and a 1GB document sample. We'll output per-query logs (latency, grounding rate, top-k overlap) and a recommended canonical config for canary.

Happy to demo a run — Marissa, want me to set up a 30-minute tech sync with Jordan & Priya next Tue?

- Aditya
